name: CA-41
label: Safe D

key_factors: Sánchez has raised $1.6 million with $416K on hand versus about $1,700 for Clemmons, leaving him without a viable campaign
The district's D+9 lean plus incumbency gives Sánchez a strong structural cushion
Prediction markets price Sánchez around 95%, slightly below what fundamentals alone suggest
No public polls of the race, so the forecast leans entirely on fundamentals
model.rationale: Sánchez combines a Democratic-leaning district, incumbency, and a roughly thousand-to-one fundraising edge, while markets still price a small chance of an upset; no polls exist, so uncertainty stays elevated despite the lopsided fundamentals.
model.watch: Any credible polling showing Clemmons within single digits, or significant late outside spending against Sánchez, would warrant moving this race toward the tossup range.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Linda Sánchez, the Democratic incumbent, advanced to the general election in a district that leaned Democratic by about nine points at the presidential level. Her Republican opponent, Mitch Clemmons, has run a minimal campaign, reporting roughly $1,700 raised against her $1.6 million, and no outside groups have entered on either side. Expert raters have not listed the race, and no public polling is available.

Prediction markets give Sánchez about a 95 percent chance of holding the seat, while district fundamentals and the financial imbalance point to a margin near twenty points. The forecast rates the race Safe Democratic, with wider-than-usual uncertainty because it rests on structural evidence rather than survey data. Clemmons would need a dramatic, externally funded surge to make this competitive.
